reason: Design bundle only, no code. `design/tool-catalogue/` proposes splitting a tool's text by the decision it serves. The measurement behind it: one tag-lane `chat` call carries 35,473 input tokens, of which 22,130 (62%) are the 54 tool schemas and 8,288 the doctrine — so the prompt is tool-schema-heavy, not doctrine-heavy, which is the opposite of what issue #305 concluded from the same symptom. The decomposition is cross-checked against the provider's own `cache_read_input_tokens` (30,080 measured against 30,418 computed, 1.1%). 54% of all description text (8,602 tokens) is result-handling prose read only after a call returns, and over 574 turns a turn uses 2 distinct tools out of 54. The bundle proposes a generated one-line catalogue for all 54 (991 tokens, measured off today's first sentences), a `load_tools` fetch verb, and relocating result-handling onto the tool result, in that order. `ToolRegistry.capability_digest()` already renders the catalogue shape for the Relevance Gate, so the generator is reuse rather than new code. Nothing here changes behaviour; five gates in `05-measurement.md` must pass before any of it is built, and two of them can stop it. Nothing a member of a room can observe.
